description: NISMOD is described as the first national-scale system-of-systems infrastructure modelling platform, developed for Great Britain by the Infrastructure Transitions Research Consortium (ITRC), a consortium of seven universities funded by EPSRC with industry partners, and extended in its second phase, MISTRAL, from national networks down to household and business level. It consists of a suite of sector models for energy, transport, water, digital communications and solid waste, an underlying database, and results that can be explored online. Version 2 links released sector models through smif, the simulation modelling integration framework (MIT licence, PyPI version 1.3.2 of 2020), with configuration, scenario, narrative and planning data to run coupled long-term simulations. The nismod2 repository holds only the smif configuration and model wrappers: prepared model data are not public, the water and energy supply models are not open, while the transport and digital models are open source on GitHub. Caveats: reproducing runs therefore needs access agreements, the framework has seen little development since 2020, and the scope is Great Britain. It supports capacity planning, interdependency and resilience analysis and climate adaptation of national infrastructure under scenarios, and runs on the DAFNI platform catalogued here.
